interest: This document illustrates how constituent casework intersected with international agricultural trade and biological quarantine regulations between the United States and Japan. It highlights the commercial importance of Japanese lily bulb exports to the American floriculture market and reflects interdepartmental boundaries, showing the State Department referring plant health and quarantine issues directly to expert officials in the Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Plant Industry, such as renowned horticulturist B. Y. Morrison.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.612 (Internal Affairs of Japan: Pests Affecting Plant Life). The docket records late-August correspondence involving Representative William T. Byrne, who forwarded a constituent request from William C. Gluckner of Albany, New York, seeking assistance in obtaining entry into the United States for Japanese lily bulbs that were already harvested and packed for shipment. The Department of State responded by advising Representative Byrne to contact B. Y. Morrison of the Division of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture, the agency responsible for plant quarantine and pest control regulations.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers indexing correspondence regarding constituent requests for the entry of Japanese lily bulbs into the United States.
subfiles.summary: This index sheet logs correspondence from late August concerning restrictions on the importation of Japanese lily bulbs into the United States. Representative William T. Byrne forwarded an appeal dated August 28 from constituent William C. Gluckner of Albany, New York, who requested assistance to permit entry of harvested and packed bulbs from Japan. On August 30, the State Department responded to Representative Byrne, directing him to consult B. Y. Morrison at the Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Plant Industry.
